result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_random_lobster()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a random lobster: a path with random legs, each of which may carry leaves. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10324-L10425){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_random_lobster( n, p1, p2, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Random lobster](/assets/graphs/add-random-lobster.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random lobsters grown from the same backbone, a path of four nodes drawn as the top row. With p1=0 and p2=0 nothing grows and the lobster is just the path; with p1=0.6 five legs hang below the backbone, making a caterpillar; with p2=0.6 as well, two of the legs grow three leaves between them, so every node stays within two steps of the backbone." width="100%"} A lobster is a tree in which every node is within distance two of a central path, the backbone. The backbone's length is drawn uniformly so that it is `n` on average (between `0` and `2 * n` nodes). Each backbone node then grows legs: it keeps adding a leg while a draw falls below `p1`, so the number of legs has mean `p1 / (1 - p1)`. Each leg grows leaves in the same way, using `p2`. With `p2=0` there are no leaves and the tree is a caterpillar. The process follows NetworkX's `random_lobster()`. The total number of nodes is random. The backbone comes first, in path order, followed by the legs and leaves in the order they grow. Every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one in a directed graph: along the backbone and outward to the legs and leaves. With probability about `1 / (4 * n)` the backbone is empty, and nothing is added. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random lobsters are useful for: - test trees with a long spine and short side branches, e.g. for tree-width or graceful-labeling experiments - modeling branching structures such as river networks with tributaries - exercising tree algorithms on shapes between a path and a star ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Expected number of backbone nodes. [p1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of adding each further leg to a backbone node. Must be at least `0` and less than `1`. [p2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of adding each further leaf to a leg. Must be at least `0` and less than `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative, or `p1=` or `p2=` is not at least `0` and less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A lobster is always a tree, whatever its size: ::: {#a31745fa .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_random_lobster(n=8, p1=0.6, p2=0.4, seed=1) graph.count_nodes(), graph.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (25, True) ``` ::: ::: Every node is within two steps of the backbone, so the leaves hang at most two edges away from it. The degrees show the branching: ::: {#11feafa4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sorted(graph.degrees(return_dict=True).values(), reverse=True)[:8] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [5, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2] ``` ::: :::
